jobs.occupation: Senior Immersion Engineer
jobs.description:
Join a project that’s not just exciting—it’s world-changing! We’re looking for talented individuals to be part of something truly remarkable. If you’re driven by challenge and the chance to make a lasting impact, this is the perfect place for you. Don’t just be a part of the future—help create it.

About FLC:

At Femern Link Contractors (FLC), we are responsible for designing and constructing the immersed tunnel, portals and ramps on both ends of the tunnel, in Rødbyhavn and Puttgarden.

We are also building the facilities for prefabricating tunnel elements as well as accommodation facilities, also known as the “Tunnel village” in Rødbyhavn, which provides housing for FLC workers.

About the department:

The immersion engineering team is looking for a naval architect, maritime engineer or offshore engineer to strengthen the team. Immersion engineering is taking care of all calculations regarding tunnel elements float up (weight analysis, determine ballast concrete and water, longitudinal section forces, floating stability), transfers in basins and harbor (winch operations with or without vessel assistance), mooring of the tunnel elements, transport to offshore location, immersion (including but not limited to dynamic analyses) and the stability of the elements after immersion.

As an Immersion Engineer, you will participate in the team responsible for floating up and/or hoisting the concrete tunnel elements, equipping them in the port and then transporting and installing them at sea. In the first phase you will participate in the preparation of this crucial operation, by making ballast plans e.g.. In the second phase, you will be part of the operational team that does the immersion work, assisting the Immersion Master by giving technical advice.

Main tasks and responsibilities:

• 
During the preparatory phase, you are responsible for the ballast plans and float up calculations.

• 
You take part in the interface management with other departments within FLC regarding specific parts of the T&I scope

• 
You will coordinate part of the design scope between Work Preparations and the design team based in the Netherlands

• 
You are involved in the management/operation of Tunnel Control Systems

• 
You ensure the conclusions and results from the design documents are correctly taken over in the work method statements, drawings and operation manuals for the Immersion Pontoon specific operations related to the overall transport and immersion scope

• 
You liaise with the Marine Warranty Surveyor and contribute to the work procedures, Go/No Go procedures

• 
During float up and ballasting you check if the operations stay within boundary conditions and act accordingly

• 
During the execution phase, you advise during the transport and installation of the elements. You will be present in the command unit of the immersion pontoons during offshore operations.

• 
You will do checks during execution, monitor the immersion process, and have an advisory role to the one in charge of the operation. You are also prepared and ready to deal with contingencies if any might occur

• 
After immersion, you will do checks on data to create lessons learned for next operations

Qualifications:

• 
You are a qualified naval architect/maritime engineer/offshore engineer with minimum of 7 years experience

• 
You have prior experience with immersion of large structures or offshore lifting operations

• 
You have a good understanding of stability calculations, mooring calculations and hydrodynamics

• 
You are a hands-on problem solver and a decision maker

• 
You are a team player with strong communication skills

• 
You find it a challenge to work in a international, multi-cultural work-environment in which communication and team spirit is key to success

• 
You are fluent in English.

Conditions: 

FLC considers transparent management structures, short decision-making channels, and a team-oriented environment to be extremely important. The FLC staff is expected to set themselves targets, achieve them independently, and take responsibility for their actions – irrespective of their position in the company.

Full time employment with health insurance and lunch arrangement available upon request.

Workplace:

Based in Rødbyhavn.

Application:

We look forward to receiving your application (in English) as soon as possible and. Applications received will be processed on an ongoing basis, and we will complete the recruitment once we have found the right profile.

jobs.occupation: Senior Sourcing Specialist
jobs.description:
Job titleSenior Sourcing SpecialistJob description:
At BeGreen, we develop and operate renewable energy projects built to last across generations. 

We are looking for a commercially driven Senior Sourcing Specialist with a strong background in renewables to lead sourcing activities and commercial contracting across solar, hybrid, and energy storage projects based in Denmark, with exposure to international suppliers and projects. 

This position is ideal for someone who understands the unique sourcing and commercial challenges of renewable energy, whether in solar, BESS, or hybrid technologies—and who knows that the right supplier relationships and contracts are what make or break a project. Broader experience in energy infrastructure, construction, or adjacent industries is equally welcome, and will add valuable perspective to our team. 

About the role 

You will take ownership of sourcing strategies, supplier engagement, and contract execution across the full renewable energy project lifecycle. Working closely with Project Management, Engineering, Construction, Sustainability, Cyber Security, HSE, and Legal, you will ensure that commercial decisions drive project performance and long-term value. 

Your hands-on knowledge of the renewables market—its key suppliers, technology trends, cost drivers, and contractual complexities—will be a distinct advantage in this role. Whether you're navigating a large EPC tender for a solar park, structuring a BESS supply agreement, or evaluating a new contractor in an emerging market, your sector insight will be central to how you work. 

Beyond large and complex tenders, you will also support pragmatic sourcing for lower-value purchases, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and speed without compromising quality or governance. 

Key responsibilities 

• Lead end-to-end competitive tenders for major renewable energy packages, including planning, evaluation, negotiation, and contract award 
• Develop and execute sourcing strategies specifically tailored to solar parks, hybrid plants, and battery energy storage systems 
• Leverage renewables market knowledge to drive supplier assessments, benchmark pricing, and identify strategic sourcing opportunities 
• Lead commercial negotiations with energy suppliers and contractors, with a strong focus on risk management and contract robustness 
• Manage both complex, high-value sourcing processes and agile lower-value purchasing activities (RFQs, call-offs, POs) 
• Prepare decision-making materials, including total cost of ownership analyses with a clear understanding of energy project cost structures 
• Support early contract management, including supplier onboarding, performance tracking, and risk assessments 
• Contribute market intelligence on renewable energy supply chains to strengthen category strategies and long-term supplier partnerships 
What you bring 

We are looking for someone with a solid commercial background, and we particularly value: 

• Direct sourcing or commercial experience in solar, BESS, hybrid energy, wind or other renewable technologies 
• Familiarity with key renewable energy suppliers, EPC contractors, and technology providers 
• Understanding of the commercial and technical dynamics specific to utility-scale renewable projects 
 Broader energy & infrastructure experience (also highly valued): 

• Experience in conventional energy, oil & gas, transmission, or large-scale infrastructure procurement 
• Background in complex project environments with multi-stakeholder commercial interfaces 
• Exposure to long-term contracts, framework agreements, and supplier performance management 
In addition, you bring: 

• Confidence in leading negotiations and managing commercial interfaces
• A structured, proactive, and ownership-driven approach to work
• Strong stakeholder management and clear communication skills
• Knowledge of EU procurement regulations (Utilities Directive) or the motivation to build it
• Fluency in English; proficiency in Danish or Swedish is a plus
• Relocation packages are not available for this role and a valid Danish work- and residence permit is a precondition
The team you will join 

You will join BeGreen's Procurement team, a group of specialists working across category management, sourcing, and contract management. We collaborate closely, share knowledge openly, and prioritize integrity in both processes and relationships.  

 

What we offer 

• A key role in shaping sourcing practices at a fast-growing renewable energy company 
• Influence across the full project lifecycle—from early development through construction to operations 
• A collaborative, international work environment with passionate and ambitious colleagues 
• A strong focus on professional development and continuous learning 
• Office based in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen.  

About BeGreen 

BeGreen develops, builds, and operates onshore energy facilities – primarily solar, wind, and battery solutions. We are around 60 colleagues from diverse backgrounds. We design our projects to work in practice – technically, commercially, and in interaction with local communities. 

BeGreen is headquartered in Denmark and is part of Equinor, an international energy company. This provides a strong foundation and access to experience and competencies across markets. 

Our values: collaboration, integrity and ambition are applied to our projects, decisions, and the way we work together internally and externally.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
jobs.description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

• 
A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

• 
Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

• 
Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

• 
The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

• 
Good written and spoken English. 

• 
A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

• 
Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

• 
Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

• 
Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

• 
Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

• 
International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

• 
Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

• 
Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

• 
Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

• 
Two letters of recommendation. 

• 
A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

• 
The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

• 
Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Further information about the scientific content of the position is available from:

Wu Chen
Associate Professor
Department of Green Technology
SDU Life Cycle Engineering
University of Southern Denmark
Email: wuc@igt.sdu.dk

Join a project that’s not just exciting—it’s world-changing! We’re looking for talented individuals to be part of something truly remarkable. If you’re driven by challenge and the chance to make a lasting impact, this is the perfect place for you. Don’t just be a part of the future—help create it.

About FLC:

At Femern Link Contractors (FLC), we are responsible for designing and constructing the immersed tunnel, portals and ramps on both ends of the tunnel, in Rødbyhavn and Puttgarden.

We are also building the facilities for prefabricating tunnel elements as well as accommodation facilities, also known as the “Tunnel village” in Rødbyhavn, which provides housing for FLC workers.

About the department:

The TE systems are part of the scope of the Marine team as temporary measures to facilitate the immersion of the elements. In total, 79 standard (220m long, 9m high, 45m wide) and 10 special elements (38m long, 12,5m high, 50m wide) will connect the Femern Belt Tunnel to both Germany and Denmark.

To be able to float up, transport and immerse the Tunnel Elements, the elements require temporary installations. These installations ensure that the elements float, stay balanced, immerse and can connect to the preceding element. A team of mechanics and electricians will install and test these installations.

Main tasks and responsibilities:

Execute the TE systems works whilst coordinating closely and effectively with the involved (internal) stakeholders to optimize efficiency.

Plan, execute and register maintenance & repairs to the TE systems equipment:

o Pumps / Piping / Valves

o Electrical components

o Subsea sensors

o Hydraulic cylinders / Powerpacks / manifolds

o Umbilical winches / Sliprings

o Rolling equipment

Thereby ensuring operational equipment in compliance with legislative-, safety- and user requirements.

You will lead the team of technicians installing, maintaining and repairing the Tunnel Elements systems during the preparation, transport and installation phase of Tunnel Elements. Understand the functionality of the Tunnel Element systems. Troubleshoot system during installation and operation. Maintain and organize the work area (workshop and yard facilities) to ensure an orderly and safe workplace in compliance with Danish regulation, company procedures, and good work practice. Set up, select and support the TE systems team of technicians to ensure effective and reliable production cycle.

In the role of the Mechanical Supervisor, there will be interface with subcontractors, Operational departments of various disciplines and operations staff.

Qualifications:

The TE systems Mechanical Supervisor:

- Has the ability to read and understand technical drawings, working methods and working procedures.

- Plans the work ahead.

- Manages daily interface with other TE outfitting parties.

- Communicates in English (minimum B2 level) both written and spoken.

- Optimizes the usage of the TE systems team capabilities.

- Supports and coaches the TE systems technicians.

- Has excellent interpersonal skills

- Organizes daily toolbox / pre-start meetings.

- Connects the tasks to the bigger picture.

- Provides support and input on risk assessments for TE mobilization / demobilization, general tasks.

Conditions: 

FLC considers transparent management structures, short decision-making channels, and a team-oriented environment to be extremely important. The FLC staff is expected to set themselves targets, achieve them independently, and take responsibility for their actions – irrespective of their position in the company. 

FLC offers attractive employment conditions on a Danish contract according to The Danish Salaried Employees Act (Funktionærloven). Pension health insurance and lunch arrangement will be available. 

Workplace:

Rødbyhavn Denmark

Application:

We look forward to receiving your application (in English) as soon as possible. Applications received will be processed on an ongoing basis, and we will complete the recruitment once we have found the right profile.

Contact:

For questions related to the position, please contact tri@flc-jv.com, lge@flc-jv.com

jobs.occupation: Positioning Specialist - Immersion Pontoon
jobs.description:
Join a project that’s not just exciting—it’s world-changing! We’re looking for talented individuals to be part of something truly remarkable. If you’re driven by challengeand the chance to make a lasting impact, this is the perfect place for you. Don’t just be a part of the future—help create it.

About FLC:

At Femern Link Contractors (FLC), we are responsible for designing and constructing the immersed tunnel, portals and ramps on both ends of the tunnel, in Rødbyhavn and Puttgarden.

We are also building the facilities for prefabricating tunnel elements as well as accommodation facilities, also known as the “Tunnel village” in Rødbyhavn, which provides housing for FLC workers.

About the department:

The FLC Survey Department plays a key role in supporting the construction of this immersed tunnel project. The marine survey team delivers positioning, navigation, monitoring, and hydrographic survey services for offshore construction activities using advanced technologies such as multibeam echo sounders, Inertial Navigation systems, LBL and USBL systems, Fibre Optic Gyroscopes and many more. Together with over 60 hydrographic and topographic survey professionals from more than 15 countries, the department ensures accurate survey data for all project phases. The topographic survey teams support construction through stake-out, control, and as-built surveys, utilizing state-of-the-art equipment including Total Stations, GNSS, drones, laser scanners, and specialist software for planning, execution, and data processing.

Within the marine survey team, the Positioning Specialists play a key role in the immersion of tunnel elements. They install, configure and operate advanced positioning systems, combining GNSS, INS, LBL, tautwire, and distance sensor technologies to ensure the precise placement of tunnel elements.

Main tasks and responsibilities:

Prepare positioning systems for (re-)installation operations by performing maintenance, calibration, and configuration of the hard- and software.

Configure positioning software in preparation for positioning operations, such as Qinsy, Delph SP and Delph INS and project specific software.

Operate and monitor the positioning systems during tunnel element installation operations, such as GNSS (Septentrio), INS (Exail), LBL (Exail), SVP (AML) and a project specific Light Tautwire and Distance Sensor system.

Remote or on-board troubleshooting of positioning system issues.

Analyse positioning data of tunnel installation process.

Write installation-, configuration- and commissioning reports for positioning systems.

Create reports for ‘as-installed’ and ‘as-configured’ survey set-ups.

Create ‘as-installed’ reports for installed tunnel elements

Cooperate with the operational team to schedule installation and removal of survey systems.

Cooperate with pontoon and vessel crews during remote- or on-board troubleshooting.

Concise communication with the immersion master during installation of the tunnel elements.

Qualifications:

Degree, diploma, or equivalent professional experience in Hydrographic Surveying, Geomatics or Geodesy, Survey Engineering, Offshore Engineering, Marine Technology, Navigation, Positioning, or a related technical discipline

Minimum 5 years of experience with surface and/or subsea positioning systems.

Proven experience configuring, maintaining, and operating marine positioning systems during offshore operations.

Experience with working with Qinsy survey software.

Experience with USBL and/or LBL positioning systems.

Ability to configure, calibrate, and troubleshoot complex positioning systems.

Strong capability in quality control, analysis, and interpretation of positioning data.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Able to remain calm and make sound decisions during critical offshore operations.

Strong verbal and written communication skills, particularly when coordinating with immersion masters, vessel crews, engineers, and survey teams.

About the position

BanThai Restaurant & TakeAway ApS in Ringsted is looking for an experienced and motivated cook with solid knowledge of authentic Thai and Asian cuisine.

You will become part of our kitchen team and work closely with the kitchen management and other employees to ensure efficient daily operations, consistent quality and a high standard of food preparation.

The position is full-time and includes both preparation and cooking duties. We are looking for a reliable and professional employee who can work independently, cooperate with colleagues and contribute positively to the development of our kitchen.

Main responsibilities

Your duties will include, among other things:

• 
Preparing ingredients for daily kitchen operations, including washing, cutting, portioning and correct storage.

• 
Preparing and cooking authentic Thai and Asian dishes according to the restaurant’s recipes and quality standards.

• 
Ensuring consistent taste, quality, portion sizes and presentation.

• 
Maintaining a clean, organised and efficient kitchen station.

• 
Assisting with daily preparation and service in both smaller and larger kitchen operations.

• 
Following instructions from kitchen management regarding production, preparation and daily priorities.

• 
Monitoring stock levels and informing management when ingredients need to be ordered.

• 
Receiving, checking and correctly storing food deliveries.

• 
Ensuring proper labelling, date marking, storage and rotation of ingredients.

• 
Following all hygiene, HACCP, food safety and workplace safety procedures.

• 
Cleaning kitchen equipment, utensils and work areas.

• 
Cooperating with the kitchen team to ensure efficient and smooth service.

• 
Assisting with other naturally occurring kitchen duties when required.

The list of duties is not exhaustive, and tasks may vary depending on the restaurant’s operational needs. Opgaverne er baseret på arbejdsbeskrivelsen i den tidligere kontrakt.

Can work independently and as part of a team.

Can maintain quality and overview during busy service periods.

Are willing to work mornings, evenings, weekends and public holidays when scheduled.

jobs.occupation: We Are Hiring – Experienced Chef
jobs.description:
EU/EEA citizenship or valid right to work in Denmark required

Ærø Hotel is looking for an experienced, skilled and reliable Chef to join our international kitchen team.

We are located on the beautiful Danish island of Ærø, in the maritime town of Marstal. We are looking for an experienced chef who enjoys working in a structured professional kitchen, preparing good-quality food for a large number of hotel guests.

We have 1 position available.

About the position

You will become part of our evening kitchen team, which consists of five chefs working closely together.

Ærø Hotel does not operate an à la carte restaurant.

Our kitchen is based on planned production and pre-arranged menus for our hotel guests. We serve between approximately 100 and 200 guests every day.

During the day, we prepare and serve lunches, while dinner consists of pre-booked and predetermined two-course menus.

Our dinner concept follows a fixed rotation of four different two-course menus. After the fourth menu, the rotation starts again on day five.

This means that our kitchen operation is highly structured, allowing the team to focus on good preparation, consistency, quality and efficient service.

We are therefore looking for an experienced chef who is comfortable preparing food in larger quantities and who understands the importance of planning, organisation and consistency when serving many guests.

The primary working language in our kitchen is Spanish, while English is the common language throughout the rest of the hotel.

Your main responsibilities

• 
Preparing lunches and evening meals for our hotel guests

• 
Preparing and cooking food for approximately 100–200 guests per day

• 
Working with our fixed rotation of pre-planned two-course dinner menus

• 
Taking responsibility for your own tasks and preparation

• 
Working closely with our team of five evening chefs

• 
Ensuring consistent quality, taste and presentation

• 
Planning and organising preparation efficiently

• 
Contributing to a smooth and well-organised dinner service

• 
Maintaining high standards of cleanliness and hygiene

• 
Following Danish food safety and hygiene regulations

• 
Supporting your colleagues and contributing to a professional and positive working environment

We are looking for someone who

• 
Has solid professional experience working as a chef

• 
Is experienced in preparing food for larger groups of guests

• 
Is comfortable with high-volume food production

• 
Is able to work independently and take responsibility

• 
Understands the importance of planning, preparation and consistency

• 
Works efficiently and remains organised during busy periods

• 
Speaks Spanish and is able to communicate in English

• 
Is reliable, responsible and flexible

• 
Takes pride in food quality and presentation

• 
Enjoys working as part of a professional kitchen team

• 
Has EU/EEA citizenship or another valid right to work in Denmark

Previous professional experience as a chef is essential for this position.

Salary and employment conditions

Salary: DKK 180 per hour before tax.

Holiday allowance is paid in addition to the hourly salary in accordance with Danish regulations.

We offer attractive working hours and the opportunity to become part of an established and experienced kitchen team.

Start date: As soon as possible

Location: Ærø Hotel, Marstal, Denmark

Staff accommodation

If needed, we can offer staff accommodation close to the hotel.

The current accommodation consists of private bedrooms with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities.

Rent is DKK 750 per week and includes:

• 
Electricity

• 
Water

• 
Heating

• 
Internet

During the coming winter, the staff accommodation will undergo a complete renovation. After the renovation, each room will have its own private bathroom and small kitchen.

Accommodation is optional and paid by the employee.

About Ærø Hotel

Ærø Hotel is a well-established hotel located in Marstal on the island of Ærø in southern Denmark.

We welcome guests from Denmark and abroad and have an international team of employees from several different countries.

Our kitchen is an important part of the hotel experience. Because most of our guests stay with us as part of organised hotel packages, we know in advance how many guests we are cooking for and which menus will be served.

This gives us a structured way of working, where good preparation, teamwork and consistency are essential.

You will become part of an experienced kitchen team where everyone works together to ensure that between 100 and 200 guests receive a good dining experience every day.

Life on Ærø

Ærø is one of Denmark’s most beautiful and distinctive islands.

The island is known for its beautiful coastline, beaches, historic towns, colourful houses, maritime atmosphere and relaxed way of life.

Marstal has a strong maritime tradition and is a lively small town with shops, cafés and the everyday facilities needed when living on the island. At the same time, the sea and nature are always close by.

Working at Ærø Hotel gives you the opportunity to combine a professional job with life in a safe, peaceful and welcoming island community.

For the right person, Ærø offers much more than just a workplace. It is an opportunity to become part of an international team while experiencing a very special part of Denmark.

If you are an experienced chef and would like to become part of our team at Ærø Hotel, we would be very pleased to hear from you.

Please send us your CV together with a short introduction about yourself, your professional kitchen experience and when you would be available to start.

jobs.occupation: Cyber Security Consultant (m/f/d) (Cyber-Security-Consultant)
jobs.description:
Do you want to contribute to protecting energy systems of the future and secure OT infrastructure in Renewable Energy? Then apply to become part of an international and market-leading asset management consultancy within the renewable energy industry. PEAK Wind is looking for a Cyber Security Consultant, who wants to take their cyber security career to the next level and is looking to work on a diverse and exciting portfolio within wind power and other renewable Energy sources.

Trusted Advisors for Developers and Investors for some of the Largest Renewable Assets
At PEAK Wind, we specialise in operations, asset management, and project management of Renewable Energy assets and take pride in providing best-in-class commercial, financial, and operational advisory and support to our clients. We work with some of the world’s largest infrastructure investments and are proud to count market-leading utilities, investment funds, and independent power producers among our clients.

Job Content, Responsibilities, and Possibilities:
Based in one of our offices in Denmark (Aarhus and Copenhagen), or Germany (Hamburg) you will be working in a team supporting customer projects and programs within the field of IT/OT and cyber security. We are a dedicated team of mixed seniorities and nationalities with a collaborative working environment. SCADA and Cyber Security is a crucial area for our clients, who we support on both greenfield and brownfield projects. The team works across disciplines, ensuring seamless integration, operation, and cyber security of OT, ICS, and SCADA systems.

Your responsibilities include:

- Leading risk assessments of IT/OT environments for clients across large-scale renewable assets, and providing risk mitigation strategies and recommendations.
- Developing IT/OT operating models, guidelines, and procedures for renewable assets.
- Developing and communicating IT/OT infrastructure designs to our customers.
- Implementing cyber security solutions for IT and OT environments on large-scale renewable assets, and reporting to project management, customers directly, and/or other senior engineering functions.
- Adapt to legislation and regulatory requirements for the IT/OT environment. Advise on the utilisation of best practices, policies, and standards, such as IEC62443, and ISO27000.
- Build strong relationships with stakeholders, in PEAK Wind and among our customers.

What you Bring and your Qualities
We expect that you have a minimum of 2-4 years of experience from a similar position, and previous experience with cyber security functions, such as Risk Management, Vulnerability Assessments, and Security Assessments. Furthermore, experience within security systems including firewalls and security engineering is required. Recognized security certification is desirable and experience with implementation of national standards such as NERC/CIP or NIS2 would be considered an advantage. The ideal candidate would have experience with renewable energy projects and/or implementation of Cyber Security Management Systems in other industries.

As a person, you are a team player, and you thrive working in an international and diverse team with mixed cultures and seniorities. You are detail-oriented and possess strong problem-solving skills in IT/OT systems. As PEAK Wind is a global company, you must also have strong English communication skills, both oral and written. Finally, we are looking for a candidate with excellent stakeholder management skills.

Experience the Highest Degree of Involvement
PEAK Wind is dedicated to fostering a work environment that values diversity and our values of Expertise, Passion, Unity, and Integrity are materialized through our team members every day. Here you will be able to utilize your financial skills while developing a strong understanding of renewable energy assets. We offer an opportunity to get on board and experience the highest degree of involvement and responsibility in PEAK Wind’s global renewable energy team. Together with the rest of the team, you will play an instrumental part in the continued success of PEAK Wind. Above that, you will participate in an entrepreneurial environment, with a focus on cooperation and a desire to change the status quo. The position will also offer global exposure as our clients work globally.

Interested and want to know more?
If you have any questions or want to know more about the position, please contact People & Development via recruitment@peak-wind.com (recruitment@peak-wind.com) . We look forward to receiving your applications & CVs as soon as possible. Please apply through ‘Apply’ at the bottom of the page. Applications will be assessed on an ongoing basis.

PEAK Wind is dedicated to fostering a work environment that values diversity. We encourage all interested candidates to apply, regardless of age, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or ethnicity.
